from: August book, night 27 (The Lord Is My Light)
p1: David had some hard, scary days, but he trusted the Lord.
He sang, “The Lord is my light. Whom shall I fear?” David meant, “Who should I be afraid of? No one!”
When it is dark, we cannot see, and that can feel scary. Light helps us see that we are safe. That is why David called the Lord his light.
p2: David also sang, “The Lord is the strength of my life.” In hard times, the Lord would keep him safe, high up on a rock. Many years later, Jesus said, “I am the light of the world.” The Lord is Jesus!
If the dark feels big tonight, you are not alone. Say, “The Lord is my light,” and remember Jesus is near.
old: Another song says, “Heavenly Father is my light. Whom shall I fear?” A light helps us see and chases the scary dark away.
When it’s nighttime and dark, a little light makes everything feel better. We can see where we’re going, and we don’t feel so afraid.
Heavenly Father is like that light for our hearts. When we feel worried or scared, He shines warm and bright inside us.
With Heavenly Father as our light, we don’t need to be afraid of the dark or of hard things. His love shines brightly, and it never, ever goes out.
